input: This module defines a small library of TLA+ operators for representing BNF-style grammars as languages over sequences of strings. It includes constructors for singleton-sequence languages, concatenation, union, one-or-more repetition, zero-or-more repetition, a grammar type as a function from strings to sets of string sequences, and a least-grammar operator defined with CHOOSE. The module has no constants, variables, actions, temporal formulas, assumptions, or PlusCal code.

This module provides a formalization of differential equations and their solutions in TLA+. It defines what it means for a function to be a first derivative (IsFirstDeriv) and recursively defines higher-order derivatives (IsDeriv). The Integrate operator expresses the existence and construction of a solution to an n-th order ordinary differential equation with given initial values, using a choice function to select a suitable solution. The module uses real numbers and sequences, and encodes open intervals and neighborhoods for analysis, but does not specify a particular algorithm or system beyond these mathematical definitions.
output:
----------------------- MODULE DifferentialEquations ------------------------
LOCAL INSTANCE Reals
LOCAL INSTANCE Sequences
LOCAL PosReal == {r \in Real : r > 0}
LOCAL OpenInterval(a, b) == {s \in Real : a < s /\ s < b}
LOCAL Nbhd(r,e) ==  OpenInterval(r-e, r+e)
LOCAL IsFirstDeriv(df, f) ==
        /\ df \in [DOMAIN f -> Real]
        /\ \A r \in DOMAIN f : 
              \A e \in PosReal :
                 \E d \in PosReal : 
                    \A s \in Nbhd(r,d) \ {r} :
                        (f[s] - f[r])/(s - r) \in Nbhd(df[r], e)

LOCAL IsDeriv(n, df, f) == 
  LET IsD[k \in 0..n,  g \in [DOMAIN f -> Real]] ==
         IF k = 0 
           THEN g = f
           ELSE \E gg \in [DOMAIN f -> Real] : /\ IsFirstDeriv(g, gg)
                                               /\ IsD[k-1, gg]
  IN  IsD[n, df]

Integrate(D, a, b, InitVals) ==
  LET n == Len(InitVals)
      gg == CHOOSE g : 
              \E e \in PosReal : 
                 /\ g \in [0..n -> [OpenInterval(a-e, b+e) -> Real]]
                 /\ \A i \in 1..n : /\ IsDeriv(i, g[i], g[0])
                                    /\ g[i-1][a] = InitVals[i]
                 /\ \A r \in OpenInterval(a-e, b+e) :
                        D[ <<r>> \o [i \in 1..(n+1) |-> g[i-1][r]] ] = 0
  IN  [i \in 1..n |-> gg[i-1][b]]
=============================================================================

input: This module defines basic graph-theoretic structures and properties in TLA+. It models both directed and undirected graphs as records with node and edge fields, and provides predicates for checking if a structure is a directed or undirected graph. The module also defines subgraph constructions, paths, connectivity, and rooted trees, using set and sequence operations. No temporal properties or fault models are present; the focus is on static graph properties and relationships.
output:
------------------------------- MODULE Graphs ------------------------------- 
LOCAL INSTANCE Naturals
LOCAL INSTANCE Sequences

IsDirectedGraph(G) ==
   /\ G = [node |-> G.node, edge |-> G.edge]
   /\ G.edge \subseteq (G.node \X G.node)

DirectedSubgraph(G) ==    
  {H \in [node : SUBSET G.node, edge : SUBSET (G.node \X G.node)] :
     IsDirectedGraph(H) /\ H.edge \subseteq G.edge}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
IsUndirectedGraph(G) ==
   /\ IsDirectedGraph(G)
   /\ \A e \in G.edge : <<e[2], e[1]>> \in G.edge

UndirectedSubgraph(G) == {H \in DirectedSubgraph(G) : IsUndirectedGraph(H)}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Path(G) == {p \in Seq(G.node) :
             /\ p # << >>
             /\ \A i \in 1..(Len(p)-1) : <<p[i], p[i+1]>> \in G.edge}

AreConnectedIn(m, n, G) == 
  \E p \in Path(G) : (p[1] = m) /\ (p[Len(p)] = n)

IsStronglyConnected(G) == 
  \A m, n \in G.node : AreConnectedIn(m, n, G) 
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
IsTreeWithRoot(G, r) ==
  /\ IsDirectedGraph(G)
  /\ \A e \in G.edge : /\ e[1] # r
                       /\ \A f \in G.edge : (e[1] = f[1]) => (e = f)
  /\ \A n \in G.node : AreConnectedIn(n, r, G)
=============================================================================

input: This specification models an inner sequential memory/request handling component with per-process register files, a per-process queue of issued operations, and a memory array. Processes can issue requests into free registers, receive responses for reads and writes, and internally remove completed operations from the head of their queue, updating memory for writes and checking consistency for reads. The spec asserts a data invariant over the register file, operation queues, and memory structure, and defines a temporal specification with weak fairness for response actions and queue removal so that enabled operations are not postponed forever.
output:
------------------------ MODULE InnerSequential -----------------------------
EXTENDS RegisterInterface, Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets
VARIABLE opQ, mem
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Done    == CHOOSE v : v \notin Reg
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
DataInvariant == 
  /\ RegFileTypeInvariant
  /\ opQ \in [Proc -> Seq([req : Request, reg : Reg \cup {Done}])]
  /\ mem \in [Adr -> Val]
  /\ \A p \in Proc : \A r \in Reg :
       Cardinality ({i \in DOMAIN opQ[p] : opQ[p][i].reg = r})
         = IF regFile[p][r].op = "Free" THEN 0 ELSE 1

Init == /\ regFile \in [Proc -> [Reg -> FreeRegValue]]
        /\ opQ = [p \in Proc |-> << >>]
        /\ mem \in [Adr -> Val]
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
IssueRequest(proc, req, reg) ==
  /\ regFile[proc][reg].op = "Free"
  /\ regFile' = [regFile EXCEPT ![proc][reg] = req]
  /\ opQ' = [opQ EXCEPT ![proc] = Append(@, [req |-> req, reg |-> reg])]
  /\ UNCHANGED mem

RespondToRd(proc, reg) ==
  /\ regFile[proc][reg].op = "Rd"
  /\ \E val \in Val : 
       /\ regFile' = [regFile EXCEPT ![proc][reg].val = val,
                                     ![proc][reg].op  = "Free"]
       /\ opQ' = LET idx == CHOOSE i \in DOMAIN opQ[proc] : 
                                         opQ[proc][i].reg = reg
                 IN [opQ EXCEPT ![proc][idx].req.val = val,
                                ![proc][idx].reg     = Done ]
  /\ UNCHANGED mem

RespondToWr(proc, reg) ==
  /\ regFile[proc][reg].op = "Wr"
  /\ regFile' = [regFile EXCEPT ![proc][reg].op  = "Free"]
  /\ LET idx == CHOOSE i \in DOMAIN opQ[proc] : opQ[proc][i].reg = reg
     IN  opQ' = [opQ EXCEPT ![proc][idx].reg = Done]
  /\ UNCHANGED mem

RemoveOp(proc) ==
  /\ opQ[proc] # << >>
  /\ Head(opQ[proc]).reg = Done  
  /\ mem' = IF Head(opQ[proc]).req.op = "Rd"
              THEN mem
              ELSE [mem EXCEPT ![Head(opQ[proc]).req.adr] = 
                                   Head(opQ[proc]).req.val]
  /\ opQ' = [opQ EXCEPT ![proc] = Tail(@)]
  /\ UNCHANGED regFile

Internal(proc)  == 
    /\ RemoveOp(proc)
    /\ (Head(opQ[proc]).req.op = "Rd") =>
            (mem[Head(opQ[proc]).req.adr] = Head(opQ[proc]).req.val)

Next == \E proc \in Proc:
           \/ \E reg \in Reg :
                  \/ \E req \in Request : IssueRequest(proc, req, reg)
                  \/ RespondToRd(proc, reg)
                  \/ RespondToWr(proc, reg)
           \/ Internal(proc)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Spec ==
  /\ Init 
  /\ [][Next]_<<regFile, opQ, mem>>
  /\ \A proc \in Proc, reg \in Reg :
        WF_<<regFile, opQ, mem>>(RespondToRd(proc, reg) 
                                        \/ RespondToWr(proc, reg))
  /\ \A proc \in Proc : WF_<<regFile, opQ, mem>>(RemoveOp(proc))

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
THEOREM Spec => []DataInvariant
=============================================================================

input: This module defines an additional constraint and a liveness property for a system specified in the imported InnerSequential module. It introduces a constant bound MaxQLen and a state constraint requiring every process's operation queue length to be at most that bound. It also defines a liveness property stating that whenever a register entry at some process is not in the "Free" state, it will eventually return to the "Free" state; the module itself contains no actions or proofs and relies on definitions such as Proc, Reg, opQ, and regFile from the extended module.
output:
--------------------- MODULE MCInnerSequential -----------------------
EXTENDS InnerSequential

CONSTANT MaxQLen
Constraint == \A p \in Proc : Len(opQ[p]) \leq MaxQLen

AlwaysResponds == 
  (*************************************************************************)
  (* A simple liveness property, implied by the fact that every request    *)
  (* eventually generates a response.                                      *)
  (*************************************************************************)
  \A p \in Proc, r \in Reg :
       (regFile[p][r].op # "Free") ~> (regFile[p][r].op = "Free")
=============================================================================

input: This module is a model-checking wrapper for the InnerSerial specification. It introduces a bounded natural-number set MCNat and a state constraint that limits the length of each process operation queue to MaxQLen, in order to keep the TLC state space finite. It also defines an arbitrary initial memory function MCInitMem for the constant parameter InitMem, and states a liveness property AlwaysResponds asserting that non-free register operations eventually become free again and that operation identifiers in opId eventually correspond to completed operations.

This module defines the interface-level data types and type invariant for a register file. It models read requests, write requests, and free register values as record-shaped values over the constant sets Adr, Val, Proc, and Reg, and then combines them into larger sets used to constrain the state variable regFile. The specification does not define an initial condition, transition relation, or temporal behavior; instead, it provides structural type definitions and a state invariant asserting that regFile maps each process to a mapping from registers to register-interface values.
output:
----------------------- MODULE RegisterInterface ---------------------------
CONSTANT Adr, Val, Proc, Reg
VARIABLE regFile
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
RdRequest == [adr : Adr, val : Val, op : {"Rd"}]
WrRequest == [adr : Adr, val : Val, op : {"Wr"}]
FreeRegValue == [adr : Adr, val : Val, op : {"Free"}]
Request   == RdRequest \cup WrRequest
RegValue  == Request \cup FreeRegValue

RegFileTypeInvariant == regFile \in [Proc -> [Reg -> RegValue]]
=============================================================================

input: This module specifies a simple asynchronous sender-receiver interface using a handshake between the variables rdy and ack, with val carrying data from the set Data. The sender may perform Send only when rdy = ack, at which point it chooses a new value for val and toggles rdy; the receiver may perform Rcv only when rdy # ack, at which point it toggles ack and leaves val and rdy unchanged. The specification defines an initial state, a next-state relation, and a temporal specification requiring all behaviors to start in Init and then follow Next with stuttering allowed; it also states a theorem that Spec implies the invariant TypeInvariant always holds.
output:
------------------ MODULE AsynchInterface ---------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANT  Data
VARIABLES val, rdy, ack

TypeInvariant == /\ val \in Data
                 /\ rdy \in {0, 1}
                 /\ ack \in {0, 1}
---------------------------------------------------------------
Init == /\ val \in Data
        /\ rdy \in {0, 1}
        /\ ack = rdy

Send == /\ rdy = ack
        /\ val' \in Data
        /\ rdy' = 1 - rdy
        /\ UNCHANGED ack

Rcv  == /\ rdy # ack
        /\ ack' = 1 - ack
        /\ UNCHANGED <<val, rdy>>

Next == Send \/ Rcv

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<val, rdy, ack>>
---------------------------------------------------------------
THEOREM Spec => []TypeInvariant
===============================================================

input: This specification models a simple one-place communication channel with handshake between a sender and a receiver. The channel is represented as a record with fields for the value being sent (val), a ready bit (rdy), and an acknowledge bit (ack), with both rdy and ack taking values 0 or 1. The sender can send a value when rdy equals ack, flipping rdy and updating val; the receiver can receive when rdy and ack differ, flipping ack. The temporal property Spec asserts that the system starts in a state where the channel is initialized and then always evolves according to the Next action, which allows either sending or receiving. The main property proved is that the type invariant on the channel is always preserved.
output:
-------------------------- MODULE Channel -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANT Data
VARIABLE chan 

TypeInvariant  ==  chan \in [val : Data,  rdy : {0, 1},  ack : {0, 1}]
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Init  ==  /\ TypeInvariant
          /\ chan.ack = chan.rdy 

Send(d) ==  /\ chan.rdy = chan.ack
            /\ chan' = [chan EXCEPT !.val = d, !.rdy = 1 - @]

Rcv     ==  /\ chan.rdy # chan.ack
            /\ chan' = [chan EXCEPT !.ack = 1 - @]

Next  ==  (\E d \in Data : Send(d)) \/ Rcv

Spec  ==  Init /\ [][Next]_chan
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
THEOREM Spec => []TypeInvariant
=======================================================================

input: This module demonstrates how to use TLC's Print operator inside assumptions to calculate and display the values of TLA+ expressions during model checking. It defines a helper operator PrintVal that prints an identifier together with an expression value, and then uses a single conjunctive ASSUME block so TLC prints the selected values in a desired order. The spec is not a transition-system algorithm with variables or temporal behavior; it is a small utility-style module focused on expression evaluation, records, record update with EXCEPT, arithmetic, and TLC output.
output:
---------------------------- MODULE PrintValues ---------------------------- 

(***************************************************************************)
(* This module illustrates how to use TLC to calculate and print the       *)
(* values of TLA+ expressions.  It uses the fact that TLC checks           *)
(* assumptions.  (See the SimpleMath module in the SimpleMath folder for   *)
(* other examples of using TLC's checking of assumptions.)                 *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* We make use of operator Print defined in the standard module TLC. The   *)
(* TLA+ definition of Print is simply                                      *)
(*                                                                         *)
(*    Print(out, val) == val                                               *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* so the value of Print(e1, e2) is just the expression e2.  However,      *)
(* evaluating the expression Print(e1, e2) causes TLC to print the values  *)
(* of e1 and e2.  Thus, the statement                                      *)
(*                                                                         *)
(*    ASSUME Print(exp, TRUE)                                              *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* is a true assumption, that causes TLC to print the value of exp when    *)
(* it checks the assumption.                                               *)
(***************************************************************************)

EXTENDS Naturals, TLC
  (*************************************************************************)
  (* This statement imports into the current module the definitions of     *)
  (* arithmetic operators from the module Naturals and the definitions     *)
  (* from TLC, including that of Print.                                    *)
  (*************************************************************************)
  

(***************************************************************************)
(* Instead of having to type Print(exp, TRUE), we could just define        *)
(* PrintVal(exp) to equal Print(exp, TRUE).  However, when having TLC      *)
(* print several values, it's convenient to print a string that identifies *)
(* the value being printed.  So, we define PrintVal(id, exp) so it prints  *)
(* the pair <<id, exp>>.                                                   *)
(***************************************************************************)
PrintVal(id, exp)  ==  Print(<<id, exp>>, TRUE)


(***************************************************************************)
(* We now use an ASSUME to print some values.  The order in which TLC      *)
(* evaluates ASSUMEs is not specified.  However, TLC evaluates the clauses *)
(* of a conjunction in order.  So, we use a single ASSUME to the get       *)
(* values printed in the desired order.                                    *)
(***************************************************************************)
ASSUME
  /\ PrintVal("Three more cats: ",
              [cat |-> 1, dog |-> "d"].cat + 3)
  /\ PrintVal("Here's a record: ",
              [ [game |-> "baseball", player |-> "Marris", homers |-> 61]
                   EXCEPT !.player = "McGuire",
                          !.homers = @+9 ] )
=============================================================================

input: This module specifies an internal memory component that interacts with an external memory interface through request and reply actions. It models a small protocol in which each process moves through control states "rdy", "busy", and "done", stores either requests or returned values in a per-process buffer, and updates the memory state on write requests while returning a memory value on reads. The specification defines an initial condition, a next-state relation over per-process actions, a temporal specification using a stuttering-closed box action, and proves that the type invariant always holds.
output:
------------------ MODULE InternalMemory ---------------------
EXTENDS MemoryInterface
VARIABLES mem, ctl, buf
--------------------------------------------------------------
IInit == /\ mem \in [Adr->Val]
         /\ ctl = [p \in Proc |-> "rdy"] 
         /\ buf = [p \in Proc |-> NoVal] 
         /\ memInt \in InitMemInt

TypeInvariant == 
  /\ mem \in [Adr->Val]
  /\ ctl \in [Proc -> {"rdy", "busy","done"}] 
  /\ buf \in [Proc -> MReq \cup Val \cup {NoVal}]

Req(p) == /\ ctl[p] = "rdy" 
          /\ \E req \in  MReq :
                /\ Send(p, req, memInt, memInt') 
                /\ buf' = [buf EXCEPT ![p] = req]
                /\ ctl' = [ctl EXCEPT ![p] = "busy"]
          /\ UNCHANGED mem 

Do(p) == 
  /\ ctl[p] = "busy" 
  /\ mem' = IF buf[p].op = "Wr"
              THEN [mem EXCEPT ![buf[p].adr] = buf[p].val] 
              ELSE mem 
  /\ buf' = [buf EXCEPT ![p] = IF buf[p].op = "Wr"
                                  THEN NoVal
                                  ELSE mem[buf[p].adr]]
  /\ ctl' = [ctl EXCEPT ![p] = "done"] 
  /\ UNCHANGED memInt 

Rsp(p) == /\ ctl[p] = "done"
          /\ Reply(p, buf[p], memInt, memInt')
          /\ ctl' = [ctl EXCEPT ![p]= "rdy"]
          /\ UNCHANGED <<mem, buf>> 

INext == \E p \in Proc: Req(p) \/ Do(p) \/ Rsp(p) 

ISpec == IInit  /\  [][INext]_<<memInt, mem, ctl, buf>>
--------------------------------------------------------------
THEOREM ISpec => []TypeInvariant
==============================================================

input: This module is a TLC model-checking companion module for the InternalMemory specification. It defines concrete replacement operators for the constant operators Send, Reply, and InitMemInt so TLC can evaluate the internal-memory interface used by the underlying specification. The design choice documented in the comments is to model both send and reply by assigning the next internal-memory value to the tuple <<p, d>>, and to define the initial memory-interface values as a singleton set containing <<p, NoVal>> for an arbitrary chosen processor p; this module itself contains no temporal properties or proofs.
output:
------------------------ MODULE MCInternalMemory ----------------------------

(***************************************************************************)
(* This is a module used for running TLC to check the specification ISpec  *)
(* of InternalMemory.  We need to tell TLC the values of the constant      *)
(* operators Send and Reply.  We define operators MCSend and MCReply and   *)
(* use the configuration file to tell TLC to substitute these operators    *)
(* for Send and Reply.  We also define MCInitMemInt, which is substituted  *)
(* for InitMemInt.                                                         *)
(***************************************************************************)

EXTENDS InternalMemory

(***************************************************************************)
(* The operator Send is used in specifications in conjuncts of the form    *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* (+)  Send(p, d, memInt, memInt')                                        *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* to specify the new value of memInt.  For TLC to handle such a           *)
(* conjunct, the definition of Send must make (+) equal something of the   *)
(* form                                                                    *)
(*                                                                         *)
(*   memInt' = ...                                                         *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* (A similar observation holds for Reply.)  We define Send so that (+)    *)
(* equals                                                                  *)
(*                                                                         *)
(*   memInt' = <<p, d>>                                                    *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* If we were doing serious model checking, we might try to reduce         *)
(* the state space by letting the value of memInt remain constant,         *)
(* so we would define Send so that (+) equals                              *)
(*                                                                         *)
(*   memInt' = memInt.                                                     *)
(***************************************************************************)
MCSend(p, d, oldMemInt, newMemInt)  ==  newMemInt = <<p, d>>
MCReply(p, d, oldMemInt, newMemInt) ==  newMemInt = <<p, d>>

(***************************************************************************)
(* We define MCInitMemInt, the set of initial values of memInt, to contain *)
(* the single element <<p, NoVal>>, for an arbitrary processor p.          *)
(***************************************************************************)
MCInitMemInt == {<<CHOOSE p \in Proc : TRUE, NoVal>>}
=============================================================================

input: This module is a TLC model-checking wrapper for a write-through cache specification. It extends an already-instantiated cache module, defines concrete replacements for the memory-interface constants Send, Reply, and InitMemInt, and then manually inlines a refinement target corresponding to an InternalMemory specification because the referenced TLC version cannot handle module instantiation. The file checks that the resulting internal-memory-style specification satisfies a type invariant, states a theorem that the hand-instantiated specification implies that invariant always, and defines a leads-to liveness property saying that every busy controller eventually becomes ready.
output:
------------------------- MODULE MCWriteThroughCache ------------------------
(***************************************************************************)
(* This is a module used for running TLC to check the specification of the *)
(* write-through cache in module WriteThroughCache.  Because TLC version 1 *)
(* can't handle instantiation, we use module WriteThroughCacheInstanced in *)
(* its stead.  We check that the specification satisfies the type          *)
(* invariant and the invariant Coherence.  We also check that it           *)
(* implements the InternalMemory specification under the refinement        *)
(* mapping described in the section "Proving Implementation".              *)
(***************************************************************************)

EXTENDS WriteThroughCacheInstanced

(***************************************************************************)
(* The following definitions are substituted for the constants Send,       *)
(* Reply, and InitMemInt of the MemoryFace module.  See                    *)
(* MCInternalMemory.tla for their explanations.                            *)
(***************************************************************************)
MCSend(p, d, oldMemInt, newMemInt)  ==  newMemInt = <<p, d>>
MCReply(p, d, oldMemInt, newMemInt) ==  newMemInt = <<p, d>>
MCInitMemInt == {<<CHOOSE p \in Proc : TRUE, NoVal>>}

(***************************************************************************)
(* As described in the section titled "Proving Implementation", the        *)
(* write-through cache specifies Spec satisfies                            *)
(*                                                                         *)
(*    Spec => LM!Inner(omem, octl, obuf)!ISpec                             *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* for the following choices of omem, octl, and obuf:                      *)
(***************************************************************************)

   omem == vmem
   octl == [p \in Proc |-> IF ctl[p] = "waiting" THEN "busy" ELSE ctl[p]]
   obuf == buf

(***************************************************************************)
(* Formula LM!Inner(omem, octl, obuf)!ISpec consists of formula ISpec of   *)
(* module InternalMemory with the substitutions                            *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* (+)   mem <- omem, ctl <- octl, buf <- obuf                             *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* Because TLC Version 1 cannot handle instantiation, we now do the        *)
(* instantiation "by hand".  So, below is a copy of module InternalMemory  *)
(* with the substitutions (+) made, and with the names of all defined      *)
(* operators prefixed with "LM_Inner_".  (Had we used the actual INSTANCE  *)
(* statements, those names would actually be prefixed by                   *)
(* "LM!Inner(mem, ctl, buf)!", where mem, ctl, and buf would be parameters *)
(* of the definitions.)                                                    *)
(***************************************************************************)

LM_Inner_IInit == /\ omem \in [Adr->Val]
                  /\ octl = [p \in Proc |-> "rdy"] 
                  /\ obuf = [p \in Proc |-> NoVal] 
                  /\ memInt \in InitMemInt

LM_Inner_TypeInvariant == 
  /\ omem \in [Adr->Val]
  /\ octl \in [Proc -> {"rdy", "busy","done"}] 
  /\ obuf \in [Proc -> MReq \cup Val \cup {NoVal}]

LM_Inner_Req(p) == /\ octl[p] = "rdy" 
          /\ \E req \in  MReq : 
                /\ Send(p, req, memInt, memInt') 
                /\ obuf' = [obuf EXCEPT ![p] = req]
                /\ octl' = [octl EXCEPT ![p] = "busy"]
          /\ UNCHANGED omem 

LM_Inner_Do(p) == 
  /\ octl[p] = "busy" 
  /\ omem' = IF obuf[p].op = "Wr"
              THEN [omem EXCEPT ![obuf[p].adr] = obuf[p].val] 
              ELSE omem 
  /\ obuf' = [obuf EXCEPT ![p] = IF obuf[p].op = "Wr"
                                  THEN NoVal
                                  ELSE omem[obuf[p].adr]]
  /\ octl' = [octl EXCEPT ![p] = "done"] 
  /\ UNCHANGED memInt 

LM_Inner_Rsp(p) == /\ octl[p] = "done"
                   /\ Reply(p, obuf[p], memInt, memInt')
                   /\ octl' = [octl EXCEPT ![p]= "rdy"]
                   /\ UNCHANGED <<omem, obuf>> 

LM_Inner_INext == 
     \E p \in Proc: LM_Inner_Req(p) \/ LM_Inner_Do(p) \/ LM_Inner_Rsp(p) 

LM_Inner_ISpec == 
    LM_Inner_IInit  /\  [][LM_Inner_INext]_<<memInt, omem, octl, obuf>>
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
THEOREM LM_Inner_ISpec => []LM_Inner_TypeInvariant
=============================================================================

input: This module specifies a simple memory interface vocabulary rather than a full transition system. It defines the shape of memory requests as either read requests with an address or write requests with an address and value, and it defines a distinguished value NoVal chosen to lie outside the set Val. The file declares an interface variable and several constants for send/reply relations, initialization, and basic domains, but it does not define an Init, Next, Spec, or temporal correctness property. A commented-out assumption indicates the intended typing of Send and Reply as boolean-valued operators over process, data, and old/new memory-interface states, but because it is commented out it is not part of the active syntax.

This specification models a write-through cache system layered over an internal memory interface, with the original module instantiation expanded manually because the TLC version targeted by the file could not handle INSTANCE. The system has per-processor control state, request buffers, a per-processor cache, and a memory request queue that serializes cache misses and writes to memory. It specifies initialization, state-transition actions for requests, reads, writes, queue processing, and eviction, and it asserts temporal safety properties that the type invariant and cache coherence hold under the main specification.
output:
-------------------- MODULE WriteThroughCacheInstanced ----------------------
(***************************************************************************)
(* This module is a version of module WriteThroughCache with the INSTANCE  *)
(* statements removed, because Version 1 of TLC cannot handle              *)
(* instantiation.  The one INSTANCE statement that we need to run TLC is   *)
(* replaced by the equivalent definitions.  Another INSTANCE statement,    *)
(* not needed for running TLC, is just commented out.                      *)
(***************************************************************************)

EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, MemoryInterface 
VARIABLES wmem, ctl, buf, cache, memQ 
CONSTANT QLen
ASSUME (QLen \in Nat) /\ (QLen > 0) 

(***************************************************************************)
(* At this point, module WriteThroughCache contains the statement          *)
(*                                                                         *)
(*    M == INSTANCE InternalMemory WITH mem <- wmem                        *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* We perform the instantiations below "by hand".  The text below is the   *)
(* body of module InternalMemory (minus its EXTENDS and its declarations), *)
(* with wmem substituted everywhere for mem, and with the names of all     *)
(* symbols it defines prefixed by "M_".  (The actual INSTANCE statement    *)
(* prefixes the names with "M!", but we use "_" instead of "!" because     *)
(* TLA+ doesn't allow "!" to be used in a symbol name except when it is    *)
(* added by instantiation.)                                                *)
(***************************************************************************)
M_IInit == /\ wmem \in [Adr->Val]
           /\ ctl = [p \in Proc |-> "rdy"] 
           /\ buf = [p \in Proc |-> NoVal] 
           /\ memInt \in InitMemInt

M_TypeInvariant == 
  /\ wmem \in [Adr->Val]
  /\ ctl \in [Proc -> {"rdy", "busy","done"}] 
  /\ buf \in [Proc -> MReq \cup Val \cup {NoVal}]

M_Req(p) == /\ ctl[p] = "rdy" 
            /\ \E req \in  MReq : 
                  /\ Send(p, req, memInt, memInt') 
                  /\ buf' = [buf EXCEPT ![p] = req]
                  /\ ctl' = [ctl EXCEPT ![p] = "busy"]
            /\ UNCHANGED wmem 

M_Do(p) == 
  /\ ctl[p] = "busy" 
  /\ wmem' = IF buf[p].op = "Wr"
              THEN [wmem EXCEPT ![buf[p].adr] = buf[p].val] 
              ELSE wmem 
  /\ buf' = [buf EXCEPT ![p] = IF buf[p].op = "Wr"
                                  THEN NoVal
                                  ELSE wmem[buf[p].adr]]
  /\ ctl' = [ctl EXCEPT ![p] = "done"] 
  /\ UNCHANGED memInt 

M_Rsp(p) == /\ ctl[p] = "done"
            /\ Reply(p, buf[p], memInt, memInt')
            /\ ctl' = [ctl EXCEPT ![p]= "rdy"]
            /\ UNCHANGED <<wmem, buf>> 

M_INext == \E p \in Proc: M_Req(p) \/ M_Do(p) \/ M_Rsp(p) 

M_ISpec == M_IInit  /\  [][M_INext]_<<memInt, wmem, ctl, buf>>
--------------------------------------------------------------
(***************************************************************************)
(* Below is the rest of module WriteThroughCache, except with each "!"     *)
(* replaced by "_".                                                        *)
(***************************************************************************)

Init == /\ M_IInit 
        /\ cache = [p \in Proc |-> [a \in Adr |-> NoVal] ]
        /\ memQ = << >>  
 
TypeInvariant == 
  /\ wmem  \in [Adr -> Val]
  /\ ctl   \in [Proc -> {"rdy", "busy", "waiting", "done"}] 
  /\ buf   \in [Proc -> MReq \cup Val \cup {NoVal}]
  /\ cache \in [Proc -> [Adr -> Val \cup {NoVal}]] 
  /\ memQ  \in Seq(Proc \X MReq) 

Coherence == \A p, q \in Proc, a \in Adr : 
                (NoVal \notin {cache[p][a], cache[q][a]})
                      => (cache[p][a]=cache[q][a]) 
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Req(p) == M_Req(p) /\ UNCHANGED <<cache, memQ>> 
Rsp(p) == M_Rsp(p) /\ UNCHANGED <<cache, memQ>> 

RdMiss(p) ==  /\ (ctl[p] = "busy") /\ (buf[p].op = "Rd") 
              /\ cache[p][buf[p].adr] = NoVal 
              /\ Len(memQ) < QLen
              /\ memQ' = Append(memQ, <<p, buf[p]>>)
              /\ ctl' = [ctl EXCEPT ![p] = "waiting"]
              /\ UNCHANGED <<memInt, wmem, buf, cache>>

DoRd(p) == 
  /\ ctl[p] \in {"busy","waiting"} 
  /\ buf[p].op = "Rd" 
  /\ cache[p][buf[p].adr] # NoVal
  /\ buf' = [buf EXCEPT ![p] = cache[p][buf[p].adr]]
  /\ ctl' = [ctl EXCEPT ![p] = "done"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<memInt, wmem, cache, memQ>> 

DoWr(p) == 
  LET r == buf[p]
  IN  /\ (ctl[p] = "busy") /\ (r.op = "Wr") 
      /\ Len(memQ) < QLen
      /\ cache' = [q \in Proc |-> 
                    IF (p=q)  \/  (cache[q][r.adr]#NoVal)
                      THEN [cache[q] EXCEPT ![r.adr] = r.val]
                      ELSE cache[q] ]
      /\ memQ' = Append(memQ, <<p, r>>)
      /\ buf' = [buf EXCEPT ![p] = NoVal]
      /\ ctl' = [ctl EXCEPT ![p] = "done"]
      /\ UNCHANGED <<memInt, wmem>> 

vmem  ==  
  LET f[i \in 0 .. Len(memQ)] == 
        IF i=0 THEN wmem
               ELSE IF memQ[i][2].op = "Rd"
                      THEN f[i-1]
                      ELSE [f[i-1] EXCEPT ![memQ[i][2].adr] =
                                              memQ[i][2].val]
  IN f[Len(memQ)] 

MemQWr == LET r == Head(memQ)[2] 
          IN  /\ (memQ # << >>)  /\   (r.op = "Wr") 
              /\ wmem' = [wmem EXCEPT ![r.adr] = r.val] 
              /\ memQ' = Tail(memQ) 
              /\ UNCHANGED <<memInt, buf, ctl, cache>> 

MemQRd == 
  LET p == Head(memQ)[1] 
      r == Head(memQ)[2] 
  IN  /\ (memQ # << >> ) /\ (r.op = "Rd")
      /\ memQ' = Tail(memQ)
      /\ cache' = [cache EXCEPT ![p][r.adr] = vmem[r.adr]]
      /\ UNCHANGED <<memInt, wmem, buf, ctl>>  

Evict(p,a) == /\ (ctl[p] = "waiting") => (buf[p].adr # a) 
              /\ cache' = [cache EXCEPT ![p][a] = NoVal]
              /\ UNCHANGED <<memInt, wmem, buf, ctl, memQ>> 

Next == \/ \E p\in Proc : \/ Req(p) \/ Rsp(p) 
                          \/ RdMiss(p) \/ DoRd(p) \/ DoWr(p) 
                          \/ \E a \in Adr : Evict(p, a)
        \/ MemQWr \/ MemQRd    

Spec == 
  Init /\ [][Next]_<<memInt, wmem, buf, ctl, cache, memQ>>
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
THEOREM Spec => [](TypeInvariant /\ Coherence)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

(***************************************************************************)
(* We comment out the following instantiation and theorem, since TLC can't *)
(* do anything with them anyway.                                           *)
(***************************************************************************)
\* LM == INSTANCE Memory 
\* THEOREM Spec => LM_Spec 
==============================================================

THEOREM ISpec => []TypeInvariant
==============================================================

It describes per-processor cache behavior, request and response handling, read misses, writes that update both cache state and a memory queue, queued memory processing, and eviction. The spec verifies a type invariant and a cache coherence property stating that if two cached values for the same address are both valid, then they are equal; it also proves refinement or conformance to an instantiated Memory specification.

  /\ ctl   \in [Proc -> {"rdy", "busy", "waiting", "done"}] 
  /\ buf   \in [Proc -> MReq \cup Val \cup {NoVal}]
  /\ cache \in [Proc -> [Adr -> Val \cup {NoVal}]]

Coherence == \A p, q \in Proc, a \in Adr :

--------------------------------------------------------------

              /\ Len(memQ) < QLen
              /\ memQ' = Append(memQ, <<p, buf[p]>>)

  /\ cache[p][buf[p].adr] # NoVal
  /\ buf' = [buf EXCEPT ![p] = cache[p][buf[p].adr]]
  /\ ctl' = [ctl EXCEPT ![p] = "done"]

DoWr(p) == 
  LET r == buf[p]
  IN  /\ (ctl[p] = "busy") /\ (r.op = "Wr") 
      /\ Len(memQ) < QLen
      /\ cache' = [q \in Proc |-> 
                    IF (p=q)  \/  (cache[q][r.adr]#NoVal)

      /\ memQ' = Append(memQ, <<p, r>>)
      /\ buf' = [buf EXCEPT ![p] = NoVal]
      /\ ctl' = [ctl EXCEPT ![p] = "done"]

vmem  ==  
  LET f[i \in 0 .. Len(memQ)] == 
        IF i=0 THEN wmem
               ELSE IF memQ[i][2].op = "Rd"
                      THEN f[i-1]
                      ELSE [f[i-1] EXCEPT ![memQ[i][2].adr] =
                                              memQ[i][2].val]

input: This specification models a binary hour clock in which the variable bits represents an array of binary digits encoding an hour value. The module defines a helper operator to interpret a bit array as a numeric value, then relates that interpreted value to an hour variable through a temporal invariant stating that the hour always equals the value computed from bits. The top-level formula existentially quantifies an hour variable and combines that relation with the imported HourClock instance's HC property, so the design connects a binary representation of hours to an abstract hour-clock specification.
output:
--------------------------- MODULE BinaryHourClock --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

VARIABLE bits 

H(hr) == INSTANCE HourClock 

BitArrayVal(b) == 
    LET n  ==  CHOOSE i \in Nat : DOMAIN b = 0..i

        val[i \in 0..n]  == 
            IF  i=0  THEN  b[0] * 2^0  ELSE  (b[i] * 2^i) + val[i-1]
    IN val[n] 

HourVal(b) == IF b \in[(0.. 3) -> {0,1}] THEN BitArrayVal(b) 
                                         ELSE 99 
 
IR(b, h) == [](h = HourVal(b))

BHC  ==  \EE hr : IR(bits, hr) /\ H(hr)!HC
=============================================================================

input: This specification models a refinement relationship between two channel instances, a low-level bit channel and a high-level channel carrying values in 1..12. The inner module introduces a state variable bitsSent and accumulates up to three transmitted bits, converting a completed bit sequence into a natural number with BitSeqToNat and forwarding it on the high-level channel. It also models an error behavior in which the low-level channel changes unexpectedly while no send or receive is occurring, forcing the high-level channel state to ErrorVal; the temporal properties define the inner behavior and then existentially hide bitsSent to obtain the overall refinement formula IR.
output:
--------------------------- MODULE ChannelRefinement ------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences
VARIABLES h, l

ErrorVal ==  CHOOSE v : v \notin [val : 1..12, rdy : {0, 1}, ack : {0, 1}]

BitSeqToNat[s \in Seq({0,1})] ==
   IF  s = << >>  THEN  0  ELSE  Head(s) + 2 * BitSeqToNat[Tail(s)]

H == INSTANCE Channel WITH chan <- h, Data <- 1..12
L == INSTANCE Channel WITH chan <- l, Data <- {0,1}
  ---------------------------- MODULE Inner ---------------------------------
  VARIABLE bitsSent

  Init == /\ bitsSent = << >>
          /\ IF L!Init THEN H!Init
                       ELSE h = ErrorVal 

  SendBit == \E b \in {0, 1}: 
                /\ L!Send(b) 
                /\ IF Len(bitsSent) < 3
                     THEN /\ bitsSent' = <<b>> \o bitsSent
                          /\ UNCHANGED h 
                     ELSE /\ bitsSent'= <<>>
                          /\ H!Send(BitSeqToNat[<<b>> \o bitsSent])

  RcvBit == /\ L!Rcv 
            /\ IF bitsSent = << >> THEN H!Rcv  
                                   ELSE UNCHANGED h 
            /\ UNCHANGED bitsSent

  Error == /\ l' # l
           /\ ~((\E b \in {0,1} : L!Send(b)) \/ L!Rcv) 
           /\ h' = ErrorVal

  Next == SendBit \/ RcvBit \/ Error 

  InnerIR == Init /\ [][Next]_<<l,h,bitsSent>>
  ===========================================================================
I(bitsSent) == INSTANCE Inner 
IR == \EE bitsSent : I(bitsSent)!InnerIR
=============================================================================

input: This specification models a simple two-phase handshake communication channel using a single variable 'chan' that is a record with fields 'val', 'rdy', and 'ack'. The channel transmits values from the set 'Data' using a protocol where the sender updates the value and toggles the ready bit, and the receiver acknowledges by toggling the ack bit. The system ensures that the channel variable always satisfies the type invariant, and the main temporal property asserts that this invariant is always maintained throughout execution. The model is basic, with no explicit fault model or fairness conditions, and verifies safety via a single theorem.
output:
-------------------------- MODULE Channel -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANT Data
VARIABLE chan 

TypeInvariant  ==  chan \in [val : Data,  rdy : {0, 1},  ack : {0, 1}]
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

            /\ chan' = [chan EXCEPT !.val = d, !.rdy = 1 - @]

Rcv     ==  /\ chan.rdy # chan.ack
            /\ chan' = [chan EXCEPT !.ack = 1 - @]

Next  ==  (\E d \in Data : Send(d)) \/ Rcv

input: This specification models a composite FIFO-style communication system built by connecting a sender, an inner buffer, and a receiver through channel interfaces. The top-level module instantiates a Channel module twice, once for the input side and once for the output side, and also defines an inner module that represents a queue-based buffer with receive and send actions over those channels. The specification asserts structural channel constraints on the records in and out, constrains acknowledgement and ready fields to match, and composes the Sender, existentially quantified Buffer, and Receiver behaviors into the overall Spec; it does not include explicit fault modeling or proof scripts.
output:
--------------------------- MODULE CompositeFIFO ---------------------------- 
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences
CONSTANT Message
VARIABLES in, out
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
InChan  == INSTANCE Channel WITH Data <- Message, chan <- in
OutChan == INSTANCE Channel WITH Data <- Message, chan <- out
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
SenderInit == (in.rdy \in BOOLEAN) /\ (in.val \in Message)
Sender == 
  SenderInit /\ [][\E msg \in Message : InChan!Send(msg)]_<<in.val, in.rdy>>
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ---------------------------- MODULE InnerBuf ------------------------------ 
  VARIABLE q
  BufferInit == /\ in.ack \in BOOLEAN
                /\ q = << >>
                /\ (out.rdy \in BOOLEAN) /\ (out.val \in Message)

  BufRcv == /\ InChan!Rcv
            /\ q' = Append(q, in.val) 
            /\ UNCHANGED <<out.val, out.rdy>>

  BufSend == /\ q # << >>
             /\ OutChan!Send(Head(q))
             /\ q' = Tail(q)
             /\ UNCHANGED in.ack

  InnerBuffer == 
    BufferInit /\ [][BufRcv \/ BufSend]_<<in.ack, q, out.val, out.rdy>>
  ===========================================================================
Buf(q) == INSTANCE InnerBuf
Buffer == \EE q : Buf(q)!InnerBuffer
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
ReceiverInit == out.ack \in BOOLEAN
Receiver == ReceiverInit /\ [][OutChan!Rcv]_<<in.val, in.rdy>>
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
IsChannel(c) == c = [ack |-> c.ack, val |-> c.val, rdy |-> c.rdy]
Spec == /\ [](IsChannel(in) /\ IsChannel(out))
        /\ (in.ack = in.rdy) /\ (out.ack = out.rdy) 
        /\ Sender /\ Buffer /\ Receiver
=============================================================================

input: This specification models a simple 12-hour clock. The state variable 'hr' represents the current hour, which ranges from 1 to 12. The initial predicate HCini ensures that the hour starts within this range, and the next-state action HCnxt increments the hour by 1 unless it is 12, in which case it wraps around to 1. The temporal property HC asserts that the system starts in a valid state and always follows the hour update rule. The theorem verifies that the invariant HCini is always maintained.

This module specifies an internal memory system that implements the MemoryInterface. The system models a set of processes interacting with a shared memory, where each process can issue memory requests, perform operations, and receive responses. The state is tracked by variables for memory contents, control state per process, and a buffer per process. The algorithm ensures that memory operations are performed atomically and that the control and buffer variables are updated consistently. The specification includes a type invariant to ensure variables remain within their intended domains, and a temporal property stating that the type invariant is always preserved by the system. The system interacts with an abstract memory interface via Send and Reply actions, and the fairness and stuttering are handled via the temporal box operator.

------------------ MODULE InternalMemory ---------------------
EXTENDS MemoryInterface
VARIABLES mem, ctl, buf
--------------------------------------------------------------
IInit == /\ mem \in [Adr->Val]
         /\ ctl = [p \in Proc |-> "rdy"] 
         /\ buf = [p \in Proc |-> NoVal] 
         /\ memInt \in InitMemInt

TypeInvariant == 
  /\ mem \in [Adr->Val]
  /\ ctl \in [Proc -> {"rdy", "busy","done"}] 
  /\ buf \in [Proc -> MReq \cup Val \cup {NoVal}]

Req(p) == /\ ctl[p] = "rdy" 
          /\ \E req \in  MReq : 
                /\ Send(p, req, memInt, memInt') 
                /\ buf' = [buf EXCEPT ![p] = req]
                /\ ctl' = [ctl EXCEPT ![p] = "busy"]
          /\ UNCHANGED mem 

Do(p) == 
  /\ ctl[p] = "busy" 
  /\ mem' = IF buf[p].op = "Wr"
              THEN [mem EXCEPT ![buf[p].adr] = buf[p].val] 
              ELSE mem 
  /\ buf' = [buf EXCEPT ![p] = IF buf[p].op = "Wr"
                                  THEN NoVal
                                  ELSE mem[buf[p].adr]]
  /\ ctl' = [ctl EXCEPT ![p] = "done"] 
  /\ UNCHANGED memInt 

Rsp(p) == /\ ctl[p] = "done"
          /\ Reply(p, buf[p], memInt, memInt')
          /\ ctl' = [ctl EXCEPT ![p]= "rdy"]
          /\ UNCHANGED <<mem, buf>> 

INext == \E p \in Proc: Req(p) \/ Do(p) \/ Rsp(p) 

ISpec == IInit  /\  [][INext]_<<memInt, mem, ctl, buf>>
--------------------------------------------------------------
THEOREM ISpec => []TypeInvariant
==============================================================

input: This specification models a joint-action memory system by composing two hidden internal components: an environment component and a memory component. The environment tracks a readiness map and can either send memory requests or receive replies, while the memory component accepts requests into per-process buffers, updates control state, and delegates additional behavior to imported operators such as Do and Rsp from an extended module. The top-level specification existentially hides the internal variables of both components and asserts the conjunction of their temporal behaviors, with each component described by an initialization predicate and a stuttering-closed next-state formula.

------------------------ MODULE JointActionMemory ---------------------------
EXTENDS MemoryInterface

   -------------------- MODULE InnerEnvironmentComponent --------------------
   VARIABLE rdy
   IE  == rdy = [p \in Proc |-> TRUE] 

   Erqst(p) == /\ rdy[p]
               /\ \E req \in MReq : Send(p, req,  memInt, memInt') 
               /\ rdy' = [rdy EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]

   ERsp(p)  == /\ \E rsp \in Val \cup {NoVal} : 
                       Reply(p, rsp,  memInt, memInt') 
               /\ rdy' = [rdy EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]

   NE == \E p \in Proc : Erqst(p) \/ ERsp(p)

   IESpec == IE /\ [][NE]_<<memInt, rdy>>
   ==========================================================================

   ---------------------- MODULE InnerMemoryComponent -----------------------
   EXTENDS InternalMemory
   MRqst(p) ==   /\ \E req \in MReq : 
                      /\ Send(p, req, memInt, memInt') 
                      /\ buf' = [buf EXCEPT ![p] = req]
                      /\ ctl' = [ctl EXCEPT ![p] = "busy"]
                 /\ UNCHANGED mem 

   NM == \E p \in Proc : MRqst(p) \/ Do(p) \/ Rsp(p)

   IMSpec == IInit /\ [][NM]_<<memInt, mem, ctl, buf>>
   ==========================================================================

IEnv(rdy) == INSTANCE InnerEnvironmentComponent

IMem(mem, ctl, buf) == INSTANCE InnerMemoryComponent

Spec == /\ \EE rdy : IEnv(rdy)!IESpec  
        /\ \EE mem, ctl, buf : IMem(mem,ctl,buf)!IMSpec
=============================================================================

The sender may send a value d only when chan.rdy = chan.ack, and doing so stores d in chan.val and flips the ready bit; the receiver may receive only when chan.rdy # chan.ack, and doing so flips the acknowledge bit. VARIABLE chan

          /\ chan.ack = chan.rdy 

Send(d) ==  /\ chan.rdy = chan.ack
            /\ chan' = [chan EXCEPT !.val = d, !.rdy = 1 - @]

Rcv     ==  /\ chan.rdy # chan.ack
            /\ chan' = [chan EXCEPT !.ack = 1 - @]

input: This module specifies an inner FIFO buffer system connecting an input channel and an output channel, with an internal queue q storing messages in transit. The module is a TLC-oriented version of another specification that originally used INSTANCE statements; here the imported channel behavior is expanded manually into prefixed operators for the input and output channels. It models channel handshaking with rdy/ack bits, queueing of received input messages, forwarding from the head of the queue to the output channel, and proves that the specification implies a type invariant stating that both channels have the expected record structure and that q is a sequence of Message values.
output:
------------------------ MODULE InnerFIFOInstanced --------------------------
(***************************************************************************)
(* The current version of TLC does not handle the INSTANCE statement.      *)
(* (This omission will be rectified with TLC Version 2.)  This module is a *)
(* version of module InnerFIFO for use with TLC. The INSTANCE statements   *)
(* of module InnerFIFO have been removed and replaced by explicit          *)
(* definitions of the operators originally defined through instantiation.  *)
(***************************************************************************)

EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences
CONSTANT Message
VARIABLES in, out, q
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
(***************************************************************************)
(* At this point, module InnerFIFO contains the two statements:            *)
(*                                                                         *)
(*    InChan  == INSTANCE Channel WITH Data <- Message, chan <- in         *)
(*    OutChan == INSTANCE Channel WITH Data <- Message, chan <- out        *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* We perform the instantiations below "by hand".  However, since "!"      *)
(* can't appear in an identifier name, we use "_" in its place.  For       *)
(* example, instead of adding the definition of `InChan!Init' to the       *)
(* current module, as does the first INSTANCE statement, we instead add    *)
(* the definition of `InChan_Init'.                                        *)
(***************************************************************************)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
(***************************************************************************)
(* Below are all the definitions from Channel, except with `in'            *)
(* substituted for `chan', with `Message' substituted for `Data', and with *)
(* "InChan_" prepended to the names of all defined symbols.                *)
(***************************************************************************)
InChan_TypeInvariant  ==  in \in [val : Message,  rdy : {0, 1},  ack : {0, 1}]

InChan_Init  ==  /\ InChan_TypeInvariant
                 /\ in.ack = in.rdy 

InChan_Send(d) ==  /\ in.rdy = in.ack
                   /\ in' = [in EXCEPT !.val = d, !.rdy = 1 - @]

InChan_Rcv     ==  /\ in.rdy # in.ack
                   /\ in' = [in EXCEPT !.ack = 1 - @]

InChan_Next  ==  (\E d \in Message : InChan_Send(d)) \/ InChan_Rcv

InChan_Spec  ==  InChan_Init /\ [][InChan_Next]_in
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
(***************************************************************************)
(* Below are all the definitions from Channel, except with `out'            *)
(* substituted for `chan', with `Message' substituted for `Data', and with *)
(* "OutChan_" prepended to the names of all defined symbols.               *)
(***************************************************************************)
OutChan_TypeInvariant  ==  out \in [val : Message,  rdy : {0, 1},  ack : {0, 1}]

OutChan_Init  ==  /\ OutChan_TypeInvariant
                  /\ out.ack = out.rdy 

OutChan_Send(d) ==  /\ out.rdy = out.ack
                    /\ out' = [out EXCEPT !.val = d, !.rdy = 1 - @]

OutChan_Rcv     ==  /\ out.rdy # out.ack
                    /\ out' = [out EXCEPT !.ack = 1 - @]

OutChan_Next  ==  (\E d \in Message : OutChan_Send(d)) \/ OutChan_Rcv

OutChan_Spec  ==  OutChan_Init /\ [][OutChan_Next]_out
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
(***************************************************************************)
(* The rest of the module is the same as module InnerFIFO, except that     *)
(* each "!" is replaced by "_".                                            *)
(***************************************************************************)
Init == /\ InChan_Init
        /\ OutChan_Init
        /\ q = << >>

TypeInvariant  ==  /\ InChan_TypeInvariant
                   /\ OutChan_TypeInvariant
                   /\ q \in Seq(Message)

SSend(msg)  ==  /\ InChan_Send(msg)       \* Send msg on channel `in'.
                /\ UNCHANGED <<out, q>>

BufRcv == /\ InChan_Rcv              \* Receive message from channel `in'.
          /\ q' = Append(q, in.val)  \*   and append it to tail of q.
          /\ UNCHANGED out

BufSend == /\ q # << >>               \* Enabled only if q is nonempty.
           /\ OutChan_Send(Head(q))   \* Send Head(q) on channel `out'
           /\ q' = Tail(q)            \*   and remove it from q.
           /\ UNCHANGED in

RRcv == /\ OutChan_Rcv          \* Receive message from channel `out'.
        /\ UNCHANGED <<in, q>>

Next == \/ \E msg \in Message : SSend(msg)
        \/ BufRcv
        \/ BufSend
        \/ RRcv 

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<in, out, q>>
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
THEOREM Spec => []TypeInvariant
=============================================================================

input: This module defines a TLC-specific state constraint for model checking an instanced inner FIFO specification without modifying the underlying specification module. The comments explain that the underlying FIFO spec has an unbounded state space because the queue q can grow arbitrarily large, so this wrapper module introduces a constant bound qLen and a predicate qConstraint that restricts the queue length to be at most qLen. The file does not define the FIFO algorithm itself, any actions, or temporal properties; it only adds a finite-state constraint intended to be referenced from a TLC configuration.

--------------------------- MODULE MCInnerFIFO -----------------------------

(***************************************************************************)
(* To run TLC on module InnerFIFOInstanced, we need to define an           *)
(* additional operator.  We don't want to modify module InnerFIFOInstanced *)
(* for the benefit of TLC, so we put the definition in this module, which  *)
(* EXTENDS module InnerFIFOInstanced.                                      *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* The specification Spec of module InnerFIFO has an unbounded number of   *)
(* reachable states, since the queue q can become arbitrarily large.  To   *)
(* model-check the specification, we have to constrain the set of states   *)
(* examined by TLC to be finite.  We do this by telling TLC to look only   *)
(* at states in which q has a fixed maximum length.  We define qConstraint *)
(* to be a state predicate asserting this constraint, and tell TLC (with   *)
(* the configuration file) to use qConstraint as a constraint.             *)
(***************************************************************************)
EXTENDS InnerFIFOInstanced

CONSTANT qLen
  (*************************************************************************)
  (* Instead of putting a fixed maximum length for q in the definition of  *)
  (* qConstraint, we let that maximum length be the constant qLen.  We     *)
  (* assign a value to qLen in the configuration file.  This allows us to  *)
  (* control the size of the model we check by changing only the           *)
  (* configuration file.                                                   *)
  (*************************************************************************)

qConstraint == Len(q) \leq qLen
  (*************************************************************************)
  (* This is the predicate constraining the length of q.                   *)
  (*************************************************************************)
=============================================================================

  /\ ctl' = [ctl EXCEPT ![p] = "done"] 
  /\ UNCHANGED memInt 

Rsp(p) == /\ ctl[p] = "done"
          /\ Reply(p, buf[p], memInt, memInt')
          /\ ctl' = [ctl EXCEPT ![p]= "rdy"]
          /\ UNCHANGED <<mem, buf>> 

INext == \E p \in Proc: Req(p) \/ Do(p) \/ Rsp(p) 

ISpec == IInit  /\  [][INext]_<<memInt, mem, ctl, buf>>
--------------------------------------------------------------
THEOREM ISpec => []TypeInvariant
==============================================================

input: This module is a TLC support module for model checking the specification of LiveInternalMemory. It provides concrete replacements for the constant operators Send, Reply, and InitMemInt so that TLC can evaluate transitions involving the internal memory interface, and it also defines a liveness formula requiring every processor to be busy infinitely often. In addition, it defines a large PostCondition value describing a specific counterexample trace as a structured record containing action and state snapshots.

---------------------- MODULE MCLiveInternalMemory -------------------------
(***************************************************************************)
(* This is a module used for running TLC to check the specification LISpec *)
(* of LiveInternalMemory.  We need to tell TLC the values of the constant  *)
(* operators Send and Reply.  We define operators MCSend and MCReply and   *)
(* use the configuration file to tell TLC to substitute these operators    *)
(* for Send and Reply.  We also define MCInitMemInt, which is substituted  *)
(* for InitMemInt.                                                         *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* This module is identical to module MCInternalMemory                     *)
(* from folder CachingMemory, except it EXTENDS module LiveInternalMemory  *)
(* instead of InternalMemory.                                              *)
(***************************************************************************)

EXTENDS LiveInternalMemory

(***************************************************************************)
(* The operator Send is used in specifications in conjuncts of the form    *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* (+)  Send(p, d, memInt, memInt')                                        *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* to specify the new value of memInt.  For TLC to handle such a           *)
(* conjunct, the definition of Send must make (+) equal something of the   *)
(* form                                                                    *)
(*                                                                         *)
(*   memInt' = ...                                                         *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* (A similar observation holds for Reply.)  We define Send so that (+)    *)
(* equals                                                                  *)
(*                                                                         *)
(*   memInt' = <<p, d>>                                                    *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* If we were doing serious model checking, we might try to reduce         *)
(* the state space by letting the value of memInt remain constant,         *)
(* so we would define Send so that (+) equals                              *)
(*                                                                         *)
(*   memInt' = memInt.                                                     *)
(***************************************************************************)
MCSend(p, d, oldMemInt, newMemInt)  ==  newMemInt = <<p, d>>
MCReply(p, d, oldMemInt, newMemInt) ==  newMemInt = <<p, d>>

(***************************************************************************)
(* We define MCInitMemInt, the set of initial values of memInt, to contain *)
(* the single element <<p, NoVal>>, for an arbitrary processor p.          *)
(***************************************************************************)
MCInitMemInt == {<<CHOOSE p \in Proc : TRUE, NoVal>>}
=============================================================================

input: This module is a TLC model-checking wrapper for the write-through cache specification from LiveWriteThroughCache. It manually instantiates definitions corresponding to the internal-memory liveness specification, using a refinement mapping from the cache implementation state variables to abstract memory variables omem, octl, and obuf, because the comments explain that the TLC version targeted here cannot handle the intended INSTANCE-based instantiation directly. The file defines initial-state, next-state, type-invariant, enabledness, liveness, and combined specification formulas for the instantiated internal memory view, and also includes constants and a PostCondition value describing a counterexample-shaped structure for model checking.

----------------------- MODULE MCLiveWriteThroughCache ----------------------
(***************************************************************************)
(* This is a module used for running TLC to check the specification of the *)
(* write-through cache in module LiveWriteThroughCache.  We check that it  *)
(* implements the LiveInternalMemory specification under the refinement    *)
(* mapping described in the section "Proving Implementation" of chapter "A *)
(* Caching Memory".                                                        *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* This module is the same as module MCWriteThroughCache of the folder     *)
(* CachingMemory, except it also "instantiates" the definition of LISpec.  *)
(***************************************************************************)

EXTENDS LiveWriteThroughCache

(***************************************************************************)
(* The following definitions are substituted for the constants Send,       *)
(* Reply, and InitMemInt of the MemoryFace module.  See                    *)
(* MCInternalMemory.tla for their explanations.                            *)
(***************************************************************************)
MCSend(p, d, oldMemInt, newMemInt)  ==  newMemInt = <<p, d>>
MCReply(p, d, oldMemInt, newMemInt) ==  newMemInt = <<p, d>>
MCInitMemInt == {<<CHOOSE p \in Proc : TRUE, NoVal>>}

(***************************************************************************)
(* As described in the section titled "Proving Implementation", the        *)
(* write-through cache specifies Spec satisfies                            *)
(*                                                                         *)
(*    Spec => LM!Inner(omem, octl, obuf)!ISpec                             *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* for the following choices of omem, octl, and obuf:                      *)
(***************************************************************************)

   omem == vmem
   octl == [p \in Proc |-> IF ctl[p] = "waiting" THEN "busy" ELSE ctl[p]]
   obuf == buf

(***************************************************************************)
(* If we extended what we did in the chapter "A Caching Memory" to the     *)
(* specifications with liveness, we would have a module LiveMemory that    *)
(* hides the internal variables of LiveInnerMemory, and module             *)
(* LiveWriteThroughCache would contain                                     *)
(*                                                                         *)
(*    LM == INSTANCE LiveMemory                                            *)
(*    THEOREM LSpec => LM!LSpec                                            *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* we would prove this by proving                                          *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* (1)   LSpec => LM!Inner(omem, octl, obuf)!LISpec                        *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* where Formula LM!Inner(omem, octl, obuf)!LISpec is formula LISpec of    *)
(* module LiveInternalMemory with the substitutions                        *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* (2)   mem <- omem, ctl <- octl, buf <- obuf                             *)
(*                                                                         *)
(* We now use TLC to check (1).  Because TLC Version 1 cannot handle       *)
(* instantiation, we do the instantiation "by hand".  So, below is a copy  *)
(* of the definitions from module LiveInternalMemory with the              *)
(* substitutions (2) made, and with the names of all defined operators     *)
(* prefixed with "LM_Inner_".  (Had we used the actual INSTANCE            *)
(* statements, those names would actually be prefixed by "LM!Inner(mem,    *)
(* ctl, buf)!", where mem, ctl, and buf would be parameters of the         *)
(* definitions.)  These definitions are all the same as in module          *)
(* MCWriteThroughCache in the folder CachingMemory, except with the        *)
(* additional definitions of LM_Inner_vars, LM_Inner_Liveness,             *)
(* LM_Inner_Liveness2, and LM_Inner_LISpec.  The definitions of            *)
(* LM_Inner_Liveness and LM_Inner_Liveness2 are tricky.                    *)
(***************************************************************************)

LM_Inner_IInit == /\ omem \in [Adr->Val]
                  /\ octl = [p \in Proc |-> "rdy"] 
                  /\ obuf = [p \in Proc |-> NoVal] 
                  /\ memInt \in InitMemInt

LM_Inner_TypeInvariant == 
  /\ omem \in [Adr->Val]
  /\ octl \in [Proc -> {"rdy", "busy","done"}] 
  /\ obuf \in [Proc -> MReq \cup Val \cup {NoVal}]

LM_Inner_Req(p) == /\ octl[p] = "rdy" 
          /\ \E req \in  MReq : 
                /\ Send(p, req, memInt, memInt') 
                /\ obuf' = [obuf EXCEPT ![p] = req]
                /\ octl' = [octl EXCEPT ![p] = "busy"]
          /\ UNCHANGED omem 

LM_Inner_Do(p) == 
  /\ octl[p] = "busy" 
  /\ omem' = IF obuf[p].op = "Wr"
              THEN [omem EXCEPT ![obuf[p].adr] = obuf[p].val] 
              ELSE omem 
  /\ obuf' = [obuf EXCEPT ![p] = IF obuf[p].op = "Wr"
                                  THEN NoVal
                                  ELSE omem[obuf[p].adr]]
  /\ octl' = [octl EXCEPT ![p] = "done"] 
  /\ UNCHANGED memInt 

LM_Inner_Rsp(p) == /\ octl[p] = "done"
                   /\ Reply(p, obuf[p], memInt, memInt')
                   /\ octl' = [octl EXCEPT ![p]= "rdy"]
                   /\ UNCHANGED <<omem, obuf>> 

LM_Inner_INext == 
     \E p \in Proc: LM_Inner_Req(p) \/ LM_Inner_Do(p) \/ LM_Inner_Rsp(p) 

LM_Inner_ISpec == 
    LM_Inner_IInit  /\  [][LM_Inner_INext]_<<memInt, omem, octl, obuf>>

LM_Inner_vars == <<memInt, omem, octl, obuf>>


LM_Inner_EnabledDo(p)  == octl[p] = "busy" 
  (*************************************************************************)
  (* The instantiation of ENABLED Do(p).  See the section titled           *)
  (* "Refinement Mappings and Fairness".                                   *)
  (*************************************************************************)
  
LM_Inner_EnabledRsp(p) == octl[p] = "done"
  (*************************************************************************)
  (* The instantiation of ENABLED Rsp(p).  See the section titled          *)
  (* "Refinement Mappings and Fairness".                                   *)
  (*************************************************************************)


(***************************************************************************)
(* See the See the section titled "Refinement Mappings and Fairness".  for *)
(* an explanation of why the following are the appropriate definitions of  *)
(* LM_Inner_Liveness and LM_Inner_Liveness2.                               *)
(***************************************************************************)
LM_Inner_Liveness == 
  \A p \in Proc : 
    /\ []<>~LM_Inner_EnabledDo(p) \/ []<><<LM_Inner_Do(p)>>_LM_Inner_vars
    /\ []<>~LM_Inner_EnabledRsp(p) \/ []<><<LM_Inner_Rsp(p)>>_LM_Inner_vars

LM_Inner_Liveness2 == 
  \A p \in Proc : 
    \/ []<>~(LM_Inner_EnabledDo(p) \/ LM_Inner_EnabledRsp(p))
    \/ []<><<LM_Inner_Do(p) \/ LM_Inner_Rsp(p)>>_LM_Inner_vars

  
LM_Inner_LISpec == LM_Inner_ISpec /\ LM_Inner_Liveness2

LM_Inner_LivenessProperty == 
   \A p \in Proc : (octl[p] = "req") ~> (octl[p] = "rdy")

=============================================================================

input: This specification models a simple 12-hour clock. The state variable 'hr' represents the current hour, which ranges from 1 to 12. The initial predicate HCini ensures that hr starts within this range. The next-state action HCnxt increments hr by 1 unless it is 12, in which case it wraps around to 1. The temporal property HC asserts that the system starts in a valid state and always evolves according to HCnxt. The theorem proves that the invariant HCini is always maintained. The design is straightforward, with no fault model or concurrency, and focuses on demonstrating a cyclic counter with a simple temporal invariant.

This module specifies an internal memory system that implements the MemoryInterface. The system models a set of processes interacting with a shared memory, where each process can issue memory requests, perform operations, and receive responses. The state is tracked by variables for memory contents (mem), control state per process (ctl), and per-process buffers (buf). The algorithm models request, operation, and response phases for each process, with explicit state transitions and primed variables. The specification asserts a type invariant is always maintained, and the main temporal property (ISpec) requires that the system starts in a valid initial state and all steps follow the allowed transitions, with the type invariant holding globally. The design uses explicit state transitions and does not model faults or failures.
output:
------------------ MODULE InternalMemory ---------------------
EXTENDS MemoryInterface
VARIABLES mem, ctl, buf
--------------------------------------------------------------
IInit == /\ mem \in [Adr->Val]
         /\ ctl = [p \in Proc |-> "rdy"] 
         /\ buf = [p \in Proc |-> NoVal] 
         /\ memInt \in InitMemInt

TypeInvariant == 
  /\ mem \in [Adr->Val]
  /\ ctl \in [Proc -> {"rdy", "busy","done"}] 
  /\ buf \in [Proc -> MReq \cup Val \cup {NoVal}]

Req(p) == /\ ctl[p] = "rdy" 
          /\ \E req \in  MReq : 
                /\ Send(p, req, memInt, memInt') 
                /\ buf' = [buf EXCEPT ![p] = req]
                /\ ctl' = [ctl EXCEPT ![p] = "busy"]
          /\ UNCHANGED mem 

Do(p) == 
  /\ ctl[p] = "busy" 
  /\ mem' = IF buf[p].op = "Wr"
              THEN [mem EXCEPT ![buf[p].adr] = buf[p].val] 
              ELSE mem 
  /\ buf' = [buf EXCEPT ![p] = IF buf[p].op = "Wr"
                                  THEN NoVal
                                  ELSE mem[buf[p].adr]]
  /\ ctl' = [ctl EXCEPT ![p] = "done"] 
  /\ UNCHANGED memInt 

Rsp(p) == /\ ctl[p] = "done"
          /\ Reply(p, buf[p], memInt, memInt')
          /\ ctl' = [ctl EXCEPT ![p]= "rdy"]
          /\ UNCHANGED <<mem, buf>> 

INext == \E p \in Proc: Req(p) \/ Do(p) \/ Rsp(p) 

ISpec == IInit  /\  [][INext]_<<memInt, mem, ctl, buf>>
--------------------------------------------------------------
THEOREM ISpec => []TypeInvariant
==============================================================

input: This module specifies a real-time refinement of an hour clock by adding a real-time variable now and an auxiliary timer variable t. It constrains elapsed time between hour-clock ticks HCnxt so that each tick occurs within a tolerance window determined by SecondsPerHour and Rho, and it also states progress/fairness properties ensuring time can continue to advance. The specification includes state predicates and temporal formulas for timer behavior, upper and lower timing bounds, non-Zeno progress, recurrence of every hour value, and an error temporal property about now remaining different from 4.
output:
------------------------- MODULE MCRealTimeHourClock --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, HourClock 
VARIABLE now 
CONSTANT Rho, MaxReal, SecondsPerHour
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Real == 0 .. MaxReal

ASSUME (Rho \in Real) /\  (Rho > 0) 

   VARIABLE t  
   TNext == t' = IF HCnxt THEN 0 ELSE t+(now'-now) 
   IsTimer == (t = 0)  /\  [][TNext]_<<t,hr,now>>
   MaxTime == [](t \leq  SecondsPerHour + Rho)  
   MinTime == [][HCnxt => t \geq SecondsPerHour - Rho]_hr
   HCTime == IsTimer /\ MaxTime /\ MinTime 


NowNext == /\ now' \in {r \in Real : r > now} 
           /\ UNCHANGED hr  

BigNext == /\ [NowNext]_now
           /\ [HCnxt]_hr
           /\ TNext
           /\ HCnxt => t \geq SecondsPerHour - Rho
           /\ t' \leq  SecondsPerHour + Rho

BigInit == /\ HCini
           /\ t = 0
           /\ now \in Real 

Fairness == \A r \in Real : WF_now(NowNext /\ (now'>r))

NonZeno == \A r \in Real : <>(now \geq r)

ImpliedTemporal == \A h \in 1..12 : []<>(hr = h)

RT == /\ now \in Real 
      /\ [][NowNext]_now
      /\ \A r \in Real : WF_now(NowNext /\ (now'>r))

ErrorTemporal == []((now # 4) => <>[](now # 4))
=============================================================================

input: This specification defines a real-time memory-related wrapper around an internal memory specification. The top-level module introduces a positive real-time bound constant Rho, defines an inner module in which a response action forces a process control state to become "rdy", and requires that every process satisfy a real-time bound RTBound on that response action together with the imported internal-memory specification ISpec. The top-level property RTSpec existentially quantifies the internal state variables mem, ctl, and buf and states that there exists an instance of the inner real-time internal-memory specification satisfying RTISpec; the file uses imported real-time operators but does not itself define transition-system variables or proofs.

--------------------- MODULE RTMemory ----------------------
EXTENDS MemoryInterface, RealTime_SS
CONSTANT Rho
ASSUME (Rho \in Real) /\ (Rho > 0)
 
   ---------------- MODULE Inner ----------------------------------
   EXTENDS InternalMemory
   Respond(p) == (ctl[p] # "rdy") /\ (ctl'[p] = "rdy")
   RTISpec == /\ ISpec
              /\ \A p \in Proc : RTBound(Respond(p), ctl, 0, Rho)
              /\ RTnow(<<memInt, mem, ctl, buf>>)

Inner1(mem, ctl, buf) == INSTANCE Inner
